issues.legal_issue: A judge should recuse from a pending appeal when disclosed facts give rise to a reasonable, non-fanciful apprehension that the hearing may not be fair, even without proof that the judge’s decision would actually be influenced.
material_facts: A party sought the recusal of the judge hearing its appeal after presenting documents indicating that the judge had purchased a flat in which a respondent had resided.
The judge had been informed of the alleged connection and the supporting documents.

The Supreme Court found that the disclosed circumstances could give rise to a reasonable apprehension that the trial might not be fair, without finding that the judge’s decision would actually have been influenced.
issues.conclusion: The recusal request was not unjustified, and the judge should have declined to hear the appeal in keeping with the highest traditions of the judiciary.
issues.legal_principle: Judges must decide impartially, free from personal bias or prejudice, and justice must not only be done but be seen to be done. A judge should recuse where established facts create a reasonable, rather than fanciful, apprehension that the hearing may not be fair; proof of actual influence on the outcome is not required.

predicates.appeal_pending_before_judge: An appeal was pending for hearing before the judge.
predicates.party_requests_recusal: A party asked the judge to withdraw from hearing the appeal.
predicates.judge_owned_property_occupied_by_litigan: The judge owned property in which a person involved in the case had resided.

issues.definition: When an appeal is pending before a judge, a party requests recusal, and the judge owned property occupied by a litigant, the judge should recuse.

issues.legal_issue: A single judge of a High Court cannot direct that an appeal pending before that court be transferred to the Supreme Court for final disposal.
material_facts: A single judge directed that an appeal pending in the High Court be referred to the Supreme Court for final hearing and suggested that the Supreme Court should not remand it to a High Court judge.
The direction was made without any identified authority or legal sanction.
issues.conclusion: The direction was without jurisdictional authority or legal sanction and was set aside; the proper course was to refer the appeal to the High Court’s Chief Justice for assignment to another judge of that High Court.
issues.legal_principle: A single judge has no power to direct that an appeal pending before the High Court be remanded to the Supreme Court for final decision. The proper course where the judge should not hear the matter is to ask the Chief Justice of the High Court to assign it to another judge.

predicates.appeal_pending_in_high_court: An appeal was pending before a High Court.
predicates.single_judge_directs_supreme_court_final: A single judge directed that the Supreme Court finally dispose of the pending appeal.

issues.definition: When an appeal is pending in a High Court and a single judge directs the Supreme Court to dispose of it finally, that direction is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A request for a judge to recuse, supported by material giving rise to a reasonable apprehension of unfairness, does not by itself warrant contempt proceedings.
material_facts: The appellant requested recusal and supported the request with documents concerning the judge’s purchase of property in which a respondent had resided.
The single judge suggested that contempt proceedings be initiated against the appellant and some of its lawyers.
The Supreme Court found no cause to initiate contempt proceedings for making the recusal request.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to initiate contempt proceedings against the appellant or its lawyers on the basis of the recusal request.
issues.legal_principle: Contempt jurisdiction is special and must be exercised cautiously, sparingly, and with restraint. It is to protect the administration of justice, not to punish fair comment or trivial reflections; the cited authorities include Jaswant Singh v. Virender Singh, Queen v. Grey, and the authority reported at 1974 (1) SCC 374. The Court described substantial and mala fide interference with fearless judicial action as the relevant concern.

predicates.contempt_reference_based_on_recusal_requ: A judge referred a party or its lawyers for contempt because they requested the judge’s recusal.
predicates.recusal_request_supported_by_material: The party supported its recusal request with material concerning circumstances relevant to the judge’s impartiality.
predicates.no_substantial_malicious_interference: The conduct did not amount to substantial and malicious interference with the administration of justice.

issues.definition: When a contempt reference arises from a materially supported recusal request and the conduct does not substantially and maliciously interfere with justice, contempt proceedings are not initiated.

issues.legal_issue: A judge’s order should not contain irrelevant generalisations or unsupported accusations that are unrelated to the issue being decided.
material_facts: The single judge included general observations about alleged efforts to malign judges and referred to pamphlets unrelated to the recusal application.
The order attributed an attempt to influence the judge to the appellant through a telephone call, without other supporting material on the record or an inquiry into the allegation.
The Supreme Court considered those observations irrelevant to deciding whether the judge should hear the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The general observations and comments were uncalled for and unwarranted, and the Court criticised their inclusion in the order.
issues.legal_principle: Judicial decisions should reflect objective consideration and judicial sobriety. Irrelevant material and allegations not established by the record should not be introduced into an order deciding a specific application; judicial legitimacy depends on the objective and impartial exercise of judicial power.

predicates.judicial_order_under_review: A court was reviewing a judicial order.
predicates.order_contains_irrelevant_generalization: The order included general statements unrelated to the application being decided.
predicates.order_contains_unverified_accusations: The order attributed improper conduct to a party without supporting proof or an inquiry.

issues.definition: When an order under review contains irrelevant generalisations and unverified accusations, those judicial comments are unwarranted.
